Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}+1\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int {x}^{0}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{2+1}}{2+1})+x+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x+C\end{aligned}
$$
